'''Linda J. Saif'''<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=https://cfaes.osu.edu/newsletter/cfaes-monthly/may-2017/linda-saif-elected-national-academy-inventors|title=Linda Saif elected to National Academy of Inventors - CFAES|website=cfaes.osu.edu}}</ref> is an American microbial scientist who works at [[Ohio State University]]. In 2015, she became the first female recipient of the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]] for her research in [[virology]] and [[immunology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.jpost.com/Business-and-Innovation/Health-and-Science/Rivlin-Bennett-present-Israels-Nobel-Prize-to-eight-US-scientists-and-artists-404665|title=Rivlin, Bennett present 'Israel's Nobel Prize' to eight US scientists and artists|date=1 June 2015|website=[[Jerusalem Post]]|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oardc.ohio-state.edu/fahrp/newsview.asp?id=21114 |title=Linda Saif wins prestigious Wolf Prize in Agriculture |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=2015 |website=Food Animal Health Research Program, The Ohio State University |access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref>

Saif is a [[Fulbright program|Fulbright scholar]]<ref name=akron /> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nrc88.nas.edu/pnas_search/memberDetails.aspx?ctID=20002211|title=About the PNAS Member Editor|website=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|access-date=3 November 2015}}</ref> In 2017 Saif was inducted into the [[National Academy of Inventors]] (NAI).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://viroimmunelab.osu.edu/news/linda-saif-elected-national-academy-inventors|title=Linda Saif elected to National Academy of Inventors|last=|first=|date=April 2017|website=osu.edu|access-date=}}</ref> 
In 2003, she studied the [[SARS coronavirus]] outbreak with the [[World Health Organization]].<ref name=akron>{{cite web |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-131813197.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830102157/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-131813197.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=30 August 2017 |title=Ohio scientists study animals to learn how to protect humans |last1=Wheeler |first1=Tracy |date=22 April 2005 |work=[[Akron Beacon Journal]] |via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription |location=Akron, OH |access-date=3 November 2015 }}</ref>

Saif is married to immunologist Dr. Mo Saif, Professor Emeritus, Department of Veterinary Preventive Medicine and Emeritus Program Head of the Food Animal Health Research Program, Ohio Agricultural Research and Development Center, The Ohio State University.<ref name=akron />

== Early life and education ==
Saif grew up in Ohio and was exposed to agriculture from an early age from time spent at her grandparents' farm.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gPGZJ_YuMwgC&q=case+western+reserve+university+linda+saif&pg=PA832|title=American Women of Science Since 1900|last=Wayne|first=Tiffany K.|date=2011|publisher=ABC-CLIO|isbn=9781598841589|language=en}}</ref> Saif attended private liberal arts college the [[College of Wooster]] in 1965 and graduated with a Honors in Biology in 1969. She briefly attended [[Case Western Reserve University]], before attending [[Ohio State University]] in 1970 to complete a Master of Science in Microbiology and Immunology. She then undertook a PhD at Ohio State University and completed in 1976.<ref name=":0" />
